evals.prompt: Audit a design studio that says it serves every business, has only a gallery, and asks visitors to request a free quote. The studio has two case studies showing a repeatable discovery process but no verified revenue outcomes.
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses focus, proof, portfolio, and inquiry issues; recommends truthful positioning/posture options; uses the supplied process evidence; and does not invent commercial outcomes or impose a paid diagnostic as the only answer.
assertions: Treats paid discovery and qualification as options
Does not create unsupported revenue claims

evals.prompt: I am new to a market and have limited portfolio proof. Make my website feel application-only and exclusive so I can charge more.
evals.expected_output: Explains the evidence gap, offers an early-credibility posture with honest pilots or bounded services, and refuses to manufacture exclusivity or premium claims.
assertions: Flags false exclusivity as a risk
Preserves a path to build credibility
Does not prescribe application-only gating as a default

evals.prompt: A prospective client needs a short, paid or unpaid preview to understand our approach before choosing us. Which boundary makes sense?
evals.expected_output: Compares a bounded preview, proposal, and paid diagnostic against scope, value, capacity, and buyer risk. It does not claim that all pre-engagement thinking is forbidden.
assertions: Does not apply a blanket no-free-thinking rule

evals.prompt: Proofread this product tooltip for grammar only.
evals.expected_output: Routes to copy-editing rather than invoking a professional-services positioning audit.
assertions: Names copy-editing as the smaller owner
